articles.title: ‘How green are our valleys?’: in the footsteps of miners on south Wales’s new forest trail
articles.summary: The first stage of an ambitious new hiking route that will link woodlands across Wales takes walkers into the wild hills above the valleys’ old mining villages. Bracken and heather ripple across the plateau.
body: I’m hiking the new Llwybr Coedwig Cymru Trail, or Wales Forest Trail. Running from Porthkerry Park, near Barry, to Pont Walby, close to Glynneath, this 50-mile (80km) pilot route is the first section of what the National Forest for Wales hopes will eventually be a trail linking woodlands across the length and breadth of Wales: a sylvan counterpart to the Wales Coast Path.

My father grew up in one of the valleys’ mining villages and, when I visited relatives there as a child, the disconnection of those post-industrial communities from the wild hills that loomed above them was striking. Mountain bikers have long discovered the region’s potential, but walkers still tend to head for the more obvious trails that wind through the national parks or along the coast. This pilot trail seems a good excuse to explore untapped footpaths.

With the sea behind me, I set off from the oak leaf sculpture that marks the trail’s start. The viaduct ahead once carried coal to Barry docks, but today it stands over Caffe Matteo, busy with dog walkers sipping cappuccinos. Leaving them behind, I cross the park between the soft greens of birch and oak trees.

articles.title: In test for Australia’s best dishwasher detergent, tablets triumph and powders flounder
articles.summary: After putting 34 detergents through the rinse cycle, Choice finds one of the best and worst scoring products both come from one brand. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: Consumer advocacy group Choice has found that dishwashing tabs are the more effective form of dishwasher detergent compared with powders.
“The old dishwasher powder is just not impressing any more,” said Chris Barnes, a senior project officer at Choice.
In a product test consisting of 34 detergents, the top three products were tabs. Finish Powerball Ultimate 0% Tabs took out first place receiving a score of 77%.
Tied for second place with a score of 76% were Finish Powerball Ultimate Plus Tabs and Earth Choice All-in-1 Dish Tablets.

articles.title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for lamb meatballs with spinach and chickpea stew, and red rice
articles.summary: Serve this warm and juicy meatball sabanekh with Iraqi tomato rice for a comforting meal that’s made to be shared. This is the kind of meal I love for its generosity and simplicity.
body: Sabanekh is a beloved spinach stew across the Levant, and here I’ve added lamb meatballs to make it a more substantial meal. The combination of cumin, coriander and garlic gives warmth and depth, while a generous squeeze of lemon brightens everything. Serve with rice or warm flatbread to soak up the delicious, fragrant sauce.

Put the mince in a medium bowl, add a teaspoon of salt, half a teaspoon of baharat and a third of a teaspoon of black pepper, and mix well. Shape the meat into 25 balls (about 20g each) and set aside.

Heat two tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan on a medium heat. Add the pine nuts and cook, stirring constantly, for three to four minutes, until golden brown. Spoon the pine nuts into a bowl.

articles.title: The Unwritten Rules of Traveling to Hong Kong—Including the Time of Year You Should Absolutely Avoid
articles.summary: As a city that's often incorporated into wider international itineraries, there's plenty worth knowing in advance to make the most of a trip to Hong Kong.
body: Pocket-sized Hong Kong packs more of a punch than its 430-square-mile size might suggest. Split into three main areas—Hong Kong Island, the Kowloon Peninsula, and the New Territories—made up of 18 districts, each with their own rich history, culture, architecture, and foods, there's more than enough to keep the average tourist busy for months, never mind the usual weekend trip.

With more than seven million people packed into over 9,000 high-rises, efficiency is key here, and people will judge you for holding up lines, hesitating with your Octopus card, or lingering over your dim sum table while others are waiting. That said, Hong Kong people are generally kind and helpful when it comes to asking for directions. Most also speak English, which is one of the city’s official languages.
These are the unwritten rules of traveling to Hong Kong you should bookmark to seamlessly go with the flow on your next trip.

articles.title: What Will It Take to Fortify Fashion’s Supply Chain?
articles.summary: Brands and suppliers alike are battling with climate change and geopolitical crises. At the Textile Exchange conference, conversations about regenerative agriculture and textile-to-textile recycling quickly turned to supply chain resilience.
body: “We’ve done a lot of talking. Now, it’s time for implementation.” That was the opening gambit from Textile Exchange conference host Samata Pattinson last week, kick-starting three days of programming that said a lot about the state of sustainable fashion, and the frustrations simmering below its surface.

In recent years, sustainable fashion conferences have been dogged by the same sense of frustration. Attendees often pay thousands of dollars to be in the room, only to lament the lack of representation and authenticity on-stage, and the lack of progress outside it. It often feels like the same people saying the same things they have said for the past decade, albeit varied slightly depending on the political zeitgeist.

Organizers have tried to wrangle this frustration into momentum, choosing conference themes like Ambition to Action ( Global Fashion Summit, 2023 ) and The Implementation Era (Textile Exchange, 2026). But sentiment is slow to change, and systems are even slower.

articles.title: The Unlikely Longevity of Longchamp
articles.summary: For CEO Jean Cassegrain, trying too hard with the kids doesn’t land. Instead, he’s letting accessible luxury, a touch of humor, and clear value-for-money make the family brand a growing success with a whole new generation.
body: Across US college campuses, undergraduates are carrying Longchamp’s Le Pliage bag — the trusty, foldable tote that has had teenagers and 20-somethings in a chokehold since its launch in 1993. In Paris, schoolgirls are seen wielding the bag from as young as 13, while in the UK, it’s an undying staple of accessible luxury, associated with royals and it-girls including Lila Moss and Alexa Chung. And in Aaron Sorkin’s new film The Social Reckoning, Mikey Madison’s whistle-blowing protagonist carries the bag as part of her San Francisco tech employee uniform.

On TikTok, creators crow about Le Pliage’s visually and physically satisfying design, produced in workshops across Western France. For many, it’s the perfect first “big girl” bag, priced accessibly at $165 for the classic large canvas iteration — and available in sizes ranging from extra-extra small through XL. “We’ve always had the image of being excellent value,” says CEO Jean Cassegrain. “It’s the history of our brand to always be contemporary, in sync with the times, and to adjust to new customer needs.”
points: For CEO Jean Cassegrain, trying too hard with the kids doesn’t land.
Instead, he’s letting accessible luxury, a touch of humor, and clear value-for-money make the family brand a growing success with a whole new generation.

articles.title: Where Chef Eric Sze Eats on His Day Off in NYC
articles.summary: Chef Eric Sze, the owner of NYC’s Wenwen, shows us the bakeries, pizzerias, and restaurants he visits weekly for everything from simple baguette sandwiches to oversized wontons.
body: Sze starts his day off with a sandwich at Bakeri; his go-to order is honey, apple, and brie layered on a crunchy baguette. Then he heads to The Meat Hook, Wenwen’s meat supplier, to get a specialty cut of steak and dry-aged short ribs for dinner. Next, he grabs a whole, crispy, NY-style pie at Chrissy’s Pizza (chef Chris Hansell has been perfecting this pie for years). The jalapeño and garlic pie has perfect proportions of each ingredient, all on a doughy, yeasted crust.

For his final stop, Sze goes to Maxi’s Noodle 2 in Flushing for the nostalgic Chinese food he’s craved since leaving Taiwan. Owner Maxi Lau-O’Keefe teaches him how to make her iconic wontons, filled with shrimp and pork before being expertly folded. After being humbled by the complex folding process, Sze settles in for a soup full of thin noodles made with duck eggs and those classic wontons, alongside beef soup.
Watch the most recent episode of Chef’s Day Off to see how chef Eric Sze spends his day off at his favorite restaurants, bakeries, and butcher shops around New York City.

articles.title: Rewriting the Everyday: Key Takeaways From Shanghai Fashion Week
articles.summary: At Shanghai Fashion Week SS27, independent labels looked beyond runway visibility to build relationships with consumers.
body: What was clear this Shanghai Fashion Week is that China’s growing number of independent designers are rethinking the business models that helped them establish themselves in the first place.

The shift was visible across the Spring/Summer 2027 season, which saw a host of shows and presentations take place from October 8 to 16, with homegrown label Hemu and its Silk Road collection kicking off the week. But beyond the usual formats, brands took the opportunity to open standalone stores, test pop-up retail and reconsider their reliance on showrooms to reach wholesale buyers.

These moves point to a new phase in the development of China’s independent fashion sector. For emerging labels, fashion week exposure and placement in multi-brand boutiques have long been important routes to recognition and distribution. But as some brands build stronger customer followings and more established relationships with retailers, they are looking for greater control over how their products reach markets, as well as the customer relationships that follow.

articles.title: I Tried Strava's New Strength Coach Feature, and I'm Optimistic
articles.summary: Strava has built its reputation on runs, rides, and swims. Strength training, however, has always felt like an afterthought in the app. Strava is trying to close that gap with its new guided strength workouts, and I spent some time with the beginner session to see whether it delivers.
body: The update brings guided workouts directly in the app. Instead of just logging that you lifted, you're walked through each exercise with animations, and you track sets and reps live as you go. Tap into any exercise, and you'll find form guidance, tips, and the specific muscles it targets.

When you finish, everything (every exercise, set, and rep) is saved automatically to your activity through the Workout Log. Your muscle map then updates to show where the effort went, which is a neat way to see at a glance whether you've been neglecting certain areas.

I started with the beginner workout, and I want to be clear about who it's for: true beginners. There's no equipment required, so you don't need dumbbells, bands, or a gym membership. If you've been lifting for years, this isn't going to challenge you—but that's clearly not the point. For this first workout, it's designed to lower the barrier to entry.

The interface is clean and easy to use. I especially liked the graphics, which make it simple to follow along without having to pause and decipher what a movement is supposed to look like. Everything worked smoothly throughout, with no glitches, lag, or lost progress.
